findings.message: docs/release-book.md:113-119,240-242 (brief template :28-30): there is no named authority or successor for re-freezing the combined plan after an in-scope correction. 0.4.8 needed five native attempts, each after a plan change, so this is where repeated peer/user pauses come from. 'Changed product contract' isn't defined against a product-commit change limited to tests/fixtures, so an owner can reasonably stop and ask. Edit: add a 'plan superseded' successor to the owner brief. The coordinator issues the new plan digest after change-impact review under the existing grant. The native owner retires its unlaunched preparation, reruns only the affected readiness rows, then prepares, reviews and launches with no new brief and no user go. Escalate only on a shipped-behavior or authority change. Test/fixture edits still refreeze product identity and invalidate gates under the change-impact rules.

docs/releases/0.163.0-plus.0.4.8-retrospective.md:7 says the release was 'delayed mainly by' fixture drift, preparation assumptions and receipt mismatches. That ranking isn't measured: :66 itself refuses to allocate gap time, and the largest gap (03:28:41→09:08:01, about 5h39m) contains the user-requested recovery-runtime scope (:21), whose duration is unbounded. The brief's 'upstream trigger was avoidable late fixture discovery' is also too narrow: the v3→v4 repeats came from previous-package reference selection (:25) and the EXDEV host topology (:24), not fixtures. Edit: 'Most recorded failures were harness/fixture/provenance errors; their share of the 12h41m55s window is not measured; the v1→v2 rebuild also carried user-added product scope.'

docs/recovery.md final paragraph ('For the current 0.4.8 incident, command failure is known and cleanup is unverified… prepare both targets before any new launch') is still pre-publication status text. It contradicts the new header and the brief's claim that stale recovery status was corrected. Activation item 3 ('Until those gates pass, rollback is unqualified') states no 0.4.8 outcome, and 'this proposal' wording remains. The header also asserts the matching instruction block was installed on all four hosts; the supplied facts only support operator-reported package installation. Edit: drop or move the paragraph to history, state the 0.4.8 rollback-gate outcome with its evidence path, cite the fleet report reference, and mark TUI restarts as unverified.

docs/release-book.md:276-280 offers release_ap_coordinator.py as a general fallback, but it is 0.4.8-specific and partly manual. validate_job hard-codes stdout {'tests':23,'captures':20,'busy_pairs':2} (scripts/release_ap_coordinator.py:172-173); compose hard-codes Vitest counts 22/1; validate_original requires deadline 600/grace 90 (:64). compose also needs --audit and --executor-review files, and no command producing them is named, which is the hand-written finalizer risk again. The book and the release-protocol status don't say whether current run-ap still embeds the defective receipt writer. Edit: scope the adapter to executed tooling 59d85b0 with those counts, and name who produces the audit/executor review and how. If run-ap is still defective, the smallest follow-up is to fix run-ap; otherwise the next release will need a manual gate that release-protocol's completion gate forbids.

The AP fix itself looks correct: scripts/release_ap_coordinator.py:143 now calls the shared recovery_results_match in place of strict equality, and compose copies the raw state/result bytes into leaf-records. But I wasn't given the regression body or the root test output, and the book's own rule (release-book.md:261-262,268-269) requires testing the transport chain, not only the validator. Add or confirm a regression through prepare-leaf→compose→write_ap_receipt→accept using the real adjacent pair, and confirm no downstream consumer re-compares leaf-records strictly. Record the fix commit (HEAD 927ca206 or the specific commit) as a post-publication verifier revision distinct from 0.4.8's 65585b4. Fill in retrospective:78 ('recorded when complete') with the test command and its 51-pass result.

compose requires prelaunch['coordinator_code'] == coordinator_identity() (scripts/release_ap_coordinator.py:185), and that identity includes the verifier checkout HEAD (:45-48). So any commit in the verifier checkout between prepare-leaf and compose makes composition fail, even a docs-only one like committing this retrospective. Recovering then needs fresh preparation, because prepare-leaf refuses partial output (:97-99). Edit the book/compat README: pin and freeze the verifier checkout from prepare-leaf through compose, and do docs/branch work in a separate worktree.

docs/release-book.md:131-132 ('For a changed shared recipe, prove the affected x86 path before paying for the full ARM run') is an unnamed cross-host gate. 'Changed' has no baseline, and no signal or receipt is named for ARM to wait on, so it becomes a peer pause and conflicts with the 'no acknowledgement unless the brief named a concrete decision' text at :138-139. Edit: define 'changed' as a tooling diff touching native recipe/fixture files since the last accepted tooling commit. The brief names the exact x86 stage receipt (stage + hash) the coordinator pushes to ARM, with a deadline. If nothing changed, ARM launches straight after its local review. Label this as a cost tradeoff (~59 min ARM stage span), not an authority gate.

Smallest high-yield preflight that's missing now. The same semantic label change failed three separate suites at three expensive points: the footer predicate at native v1, the HUD 'longest' assertion at v2, and the cursor predicate at compat v4 (retrospective:17,23,28). The book's 'UI/version contracts' row (release-book.md:94) states the goal but gives no check. Add to §2 and the checklist: for every changed user-visible string, search product tests, tooling recipe predicates (footer/HUD/cursor), compat recipe and the AP classifier for the old literal before freeze, and record a disposition for each hit. This needs no package and would have caught all three; a small checked-in script can follow.

release-book.md:97 and the checklist 'Producer-shaped status/export/import/acceptance' row require consumer-chain proof 'before expensive native work' but name no command or corpus. Before launch the only producer-shaped records are a --rehearsal attempt or preserved 0.4.8 records. Edit: name the corpus (minimal fixtures shaped from the real 0.4.8 adjacent-float state/result pair and the socket_removed:false + removal-seal proof) and the existing test command. Run it when verifier/tooling changed since the last accepted verifier; otherwise record 'unchanged since <commit>'. Otherwise the row will either be silently skipped or become a pause.

release-book.md:65-72 tells workers to 'Use release_native.checkout_identity', which is a Python function, not a CLI. That contradicts :165-166 ('rather than per-release scripts calling guessed private APIs') and invites the wrong-API-shape mistake from 0.4.8. Edit: name the exact supported invocation (e.g. the release_native.py verify subcommand, if it compares the full seal); otherwise add a tiny CLI as follow-up. Cheap extra guard: export GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 (or use git --no-optional-locks) in worker environments, so any unavoidable read-only Git command can't opportunistically rewrite the index. Check this on the pinned git version; it does not replace seal comparison.

release-book.md:144-146 ('A separately accepted historical artifact requires an explicit supported acceptance decision') reads like an exception route for carrying an artifact across attempts. That contradicts :284-286 and the release-protocol reuse table. Replace with: 'Reuse only via the helper-only or test-only paths in release-protocol §Changes and evidence validity; new-runner artifacts and receipts never cross attempts.'

Retrospective claims to correct: (a) managed log f09c7c61-452a-4869-bdc2-a00455ed0519 is cited as an integrated-source-check failure log (:16), but release-protocol.md (Packaging preflight root evidence) cites it as the real 7-second packaging preflight; verify and fix one citation. (b) :19 calls git status 'avoidable provenance mutation' in the first-x86 row with no evidence that git status caused that drift; the only established git-status incident is :31. Label the v1 cause as not established. (c) :27 'spent substantial time linking' rests on one observation of a live ld; say 'linker share not measured'. (d) :76 'moves future-phase prerequisites before expensive work': the book lists them, but no command enforces them (book :99-100).

retrospective:1 is still a Draft, and the ARM owner report is pending. Missing measured ARM data: the managed start/finish for native v5 2098f5c5 and compat c7c45a92 (:52), the ARM v1–v4 attempt intervals including v3 7f9e7d43, the timing of the preparation refusal and pkg-config correction, and ARM-local waits on coordinator messages. Without the last item, the 'avoidable peer pause' claim can't be measured. The retrospective can't be approved as final until the report is merged with measured/inferred labels per item.

release-book.md:255-256 says finished_at values 'can differ by one representable step after a JSON round trip'. A correctly rounded shortest-repr JSON round trip of a double is exact. The evidence (retrospective:26) shows the one-step difference, not how it arose. Edit: 'were observed to differ by one adjacent double between the raw result and the state copy; the producing step is not established.' The tolerance then rests on the observed pair plus the full identity checks, not on an assumed mechanism.

docs/release-checklist.md:12 has no field for a separate coordinator verifier or AP adapter revision, which the brief requires (product / executed tooling / verifier). Add 'Executed tooling commit / coordinator verifier commit / AP adapter revision'. The incident table's 'Time lost' column (:69) invites made-up per-incident durations, which the retrospective rightly avoids. Rename it to 'Measured interval + source, or not measured'.

release-book.md:62 (§1) says to freeze host-profile identities, but a §2 readiness correction (such as the ARM private pkg-config fix) changes the profile, and the combined plan is only frozen at the §2 exit (:118-119). Change §1 to 'record candidate identities'; this avoids a spurious refreeze round trip.

release-book.md:173 'Confirm any required AP installation with fleet' sits in §4, after captures. Move it into the §2 AP replay readiness row so it can't block late. Separately, the retrospective publishes absolute host paths (/home/liupan/…, /data/liupan/…) under docs/releases, and book :186 says local paths aren't portable proof. Mark R/ as privately retained evidence, add hashes for the key evidence files, and consider dropping absolute home paths.

next_steps: P1: Add a 'plan superseded' successor and an authority rule to the owner brief (release-book Owners/§2/Recovery). The coordinator issues the new plan digest under the existing grant; the owner re-prepares without a new brief or user go; only a shipped-behavior or authority change escalates.

P1: Rewrite retrospective:7 as an unranked incident count with an explicit 'not measured' share of the window. Generalize the repeat trigger to fixture/reference/topology discovery. Fix the f09c7c61 double citation and label the inferred v1 git-status cause and the linker claim.

P1: In docs/recovery.md, remove or historicize the final 'current 0.4.8 incident' paragraph, state the 0.4.8 rollback-gate outcome with evidence, cite the fleet installation report, and mark TUI restarts as unverified.

P1: Merge the ARM owner report. Add the ARM managed intervals (2098f5c5, c7c45a92, v1–v4), the timing of the preparation refusal and pkg-config correction, and ARM-local waits on coordinator messages, each labeled measured or inferred. Only then remove the Draft marker.

P2: Scope release_ap_coordinator.py to 0.4.8 executed tooling and its hard-coded counts. State whether current run-ap is fixed. Name the producer of --audit/--executor-review. Require the verifier checkout to stay frozen from prepare-leaf through compose.

P2: Add or confirm a chain regression (prepare-leaf→compose→write_ap_receipt→accept) with the real adjacent-float pair. Record the fix commit as a post-publication verifier revision separate from 65585b4, and fill in retrospective:78 with the command and its 51-pass result.

P2: Add the label-migration inventory preflight to the §2 'UI/version contracts' row and the checklist: search every product/tooling/compat/AP predicate for each changed string's old literal before freeze and record a disposition per hit.

P2: Define the x86-first trigger (a native recipe/fixture diff since the last accepted tooling) and the exact x86 receipt the coordinator pushes to ARM; otherwise ARM launches immediately after local review.
P2: Name the corpus and existing test command for the producer-shaped consumer-chain readiness row, or record 'unchanged since <verifier commit>'.

P3: Replace the 'Use release_native.checkout_identity' instruction with a named CLI and add GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 to worker environments. Tighten the historical-artifact reuse sentence, the JSON-round-trip mechanism wording, the checklist identity and 'Time lost' fields, §1 freeze ordering, the AP-install placement and the absolute-path publication.

Follow-up, not now: a checked-in label-inventory script; a run-ap receipt-writer fix or plan-derived counts in the adapter; and, only if documentation proves insufficient, a read-only readiness CLI that reuses the existing phase-local compat/AP preparation validators. Do not build an orchestrator or cross-attempt reuse.

A future --rehearsal on both hosts under one plan would establish only: (a) one conditional ARM brief reaches export with zero coordinator/user messages on the success path; (b) a 'plan superseded' change is absorbed without a new brief; (c) the producer-shaped chain passes from status through accept on the fixed verifier; (d) baseline-to-launch time per host.
That rehearsal cannot measure build speed or qualify a package. Build timing needs the separate controlled A1/A2 comparison already in release-protocol.

Record that these docs live on a branch based on ca350ff while local main is the older 181ca5f. Merging to main is a separate root decision; until then, operators must read the book from the selected tooling checkout.
Before the final verdict, have someone review the inputs not supplied here: the compat/README.md diff, the retrospective timings JSON, the regression test body and the recovery_results_match source.
summary:
Revise. The draft is mostly honest. It keeps failures failed, rules out cross-attempt receipt reuse and a turnkey orchestrator, makes no faster-build claim, and leaves the 12h41m55s window unallocated. Its timing figures match the brief: ARM stage span 3536.598s ≈ 58m57s, about 1124s overlap with final x86, ARM frontend/harness 1530s/1525s, final x86 native 1214s. The AP fix at scripts/release_ap_coordinator.py:143 correctly calls the shared narrow matcher.

Remaining defects:
(1) The headline sentence ranks delay causes that were never measured; the largest gap includes user-added product scope.
(2) The most repeated cost driver, a plan change after an in-scope fix, has no named authority or successor, so it stays a hidden peer/user pause.
(3) The x86-first rule is an unnamed cross-host wait.
(4) recovery.md still has the pre-publication 'current incident' paragraph and an unsupported instruction-block install claim.
(5) The AP adapter is 0.4.8-specific (hard-coded counts, no named producer for the audit and executor-review files, and compose fails if the verifier checkout HEAD moves) but the book presents it as a general fallback.
(6) The readiness table has no runnable check for the label change that broke three suites at three expensive points, or for the producer-shaped evidence chain.

The ARM owner report is pending, so the retrospective can't be final; this doesn't block the book edits. Not reviewed: compat README diff, timings JSON, regression test body, shared matcher source. Those claims rest on the brief. No new release or rehearsal is needed to finish the documents.
